transcript: He got him out and laid him on the hide in the dry grass and did the whole of it properly, wrappings off, the leg looked at in daylight, boiled water gone cold, the wrapping on again not tight. You counted them at the fire. He was a squat man of about fifty with a beard in two colors and a cart no bigger than a door with a single pony in the shafts, and the cart had four sacks in it and a coil of rope and a child's chair with a broken arm which was the part Jab could not stop looking at. He scratched under his beard. And somewhere in the third verse, out in the ditch on the left, at the edge of what the amber line could show him, something that had been keeping station with him stopped.
